Neumann coefficients, quadratic catch response and single-eigenmode sharp cutoff are explicitly derived; exact algebra and independent finite collocation validate the worked example. Claims exclude the critical higher-order sign.

originality.rationale: Aye–Bock supplies the nonlinear spatial model and homogeneous equilibrium, not the second-order fixed-mean-effort spectral yield law or global stock inequality. Hilborn et al. already establish qualitatively analogous fixed-effort movement/catch tradeoffs by discrete fishery simulation and the broad qualitative conclusion is expressly not claimed new. The exact analytic parameterized theorem survives statement/implication comparison with inspected sources and closest indexed research records, subject to disclosed historical-priority risk.
residual_risks: The full 2003 Neubert paper was not inspected; full text of Kurata–Shi 2008 was accessible as parsed PDF text but its page-image screenshot was unavailable (403). An unindexed perturbative result might reproduce the Neumann quadratic response.
The qualitative sign reversal under fixed effort and fish movement is known from Hilborn et al. 2024 and is not itself claimed original.
A fixed-time finite-horizon optimal-control Hessian might be related under a nontrivial limiting argument, but no directly dominating result was identified.

value.rationale: Fixed mean fishing effort directly isolates spatial planning from a change in total extraction capacity. The full mode-resolved formula and exact diffusion cutoff explain when the same intervention protects biomass but harms harvest versus improves both, while a nonperturbative stock bound addresses arbitrary effort heterogeneity. This is a motivated management/biology invariant rather than an arbitrary numerical slice; empirical validation and global optimality are not claimed.
